In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Mutaffifin (The Defrauders)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Woe to the defrauders.﴾

At-tatfif (defrauding, short-measuring) is reducing from at-tatfif, which means a small or slight amount.

The verses that follow explain it, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full. But when they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 2-3]

They said: It was revealed concerning a man who had two measures, a large one and a small one. When he took from others for himself, he took with the large measure, and when he gave to others from his own, he gave with the small measure. In both cases there is tatfif, that is, reducing people's rights.

The opening of this surah with "woe to the defrauders" points to the severity of this act, and it is indeed grave, because measure is the standard of the world's economy and the balance of dealings. If it is disrupted, it causes disorder in the economy and, consequently, disorder in dealings, and this is great corruption.

Greater than all of this is riba (usury), when one commodity is sold for the same kind and there is a discrepancy in measure or weight.

Concerning it, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then be warned of war from God and His Messenger.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 279]

For this reason, the mention of measure and weight appears, and the exhortation to care for them, in several places and in several styles, some specific and some general.

It is mentioned in al-An'am, al-A'raf, Hud, Bani Isra'il, ar-Rahman and al-Hadid, that is, in six surahs of the Noble Qur'an.

First, in Surat al-An'am, in the context of what is known as the Ten Commandments: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him.﴾ [al-An'am: 151] (p. 455)

It also mentions kindness to parents, the prohibition of killing children, of approaching immoral acts, of killing the soul that God has forbidden, and the prohibition of taking the wealth of an orphan.

Then He said: ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative. And fulfill the covenant of God.﴾ [al-An'am: 152]

The Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, spoke here with a concise and beneficial statement: that the command here is according to capacity, and whoever falls short without intending transgression has no blame upon him.

He said: Here He did not mention a punishment for one who deliberately does this, but He threatened him with "woe" in another place, and he cited the beginning of this surah: ﴿Woe to the defrauders.﴾

As He also clarified the outcome of fulfilling measure in His saying: ﴿That is better and best in outcome.﴾ [an-Nisa': 59], that is, in its final result.

Here the Shaykh's statement, may God have mercy on him, draws attention to an important point, which is in His saying: ﴿We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity.﴾ [al-An'am: 152], since tatfif means a slight excess, and a slight thing is a small amount.

It is as if the verse here says: strive, to the extent of your ability, to avoid even a slight shortfall.

After exerting effort, "We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity." This is the utmost in striving, together with the severe warning and the threat of "woe." If the threat of woe is for a slight matter, then what is greater than it is all the more so.

The second place is in Surat al-A'raf, in His saying: ﴿And to Midian We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said: O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So give full measure and weight, and do not deprive people of their things, and do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation. That is best for you, if you are believers.﴾ [al-A'raf: 85]

So the command to fulfill measure is linked with the command to worship God alone, because in both matters there is giving every rightful person his right without any deficiency.

(p. 456) It also shows that in failing to give what is required there is depriving people of their things and corruption on the earth after its reformation.

The third place is in Surat Hud, also concerning Shu'ayb: ﴿And to Midian We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said: O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the balance. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day.﴾ ﴿And O my people, give full measure and balance with justice, and do not deprive people of their things, and do not commit corruption on the earth, spreading mischief.﴾ ﴿What remains with God is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a keeper over you.﴾ [Hud: 84-86], and the verse continues.

In the same style as before, He linked it to the worship of God alone, and repeated the command after the prohibition: ﴿And do not diminish the measure and the balance﴾, then: ﴿Give full measure and balance with justice﴾, a prohibition of diminishing it and a command to complete it. He stated the implication explicitly with emphasis: ﴿And do not deprive people of their things, and do not commit corruption on the earth, spreading mischief.﴾ together with the guidance that what is with God is better for them.

The fourth place is in Surat Bani Isra'il: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched﴾ [al-Isra': 29], that is, moderation in spending, even with regard to oneself, let alone others. Then, God extends provision to whomever He wills. Then: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾ [al-Isra': 31], and all of these are in the field of economics. After them: ﴿And do not approach adultery﴾ [al-Isra': 32], ﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾ [al-Isra': 33].

The motive for both may also be a financial aim: ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in the best manner﴾ [al-Isra': 34], and this is among the most specific areas of wealth.

Then the fulfilment of covenants. Then: ﴿And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a true balance. That is best and best in outcome.﴾ [al-Isra': 35]. Thus, alongside the necessities of life, the preservation of life, honor and wealth, comes the preservation of measure and weight.

The fifth place is in Surat ash-Shura, and it is more general than what preceded. He linked it to the sending down of the Book in His saying: ﴿God is the One who sent down the Book with truth and the balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ [ash-Shura: 17]

(p. 457) The Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, spoke concerning this verse, pointing out that it is general, and said: The balance here means justice and fairness, and this meaning includes the instrument of weighing and more.

He cited the rest of the verses here in a detailed discussion, mentioning the verse of ar-Rahman and the verse of al-Hadid, and he spoke about all of them in detail.

In His saying in Surat ar-Rahman: ﴿And the heaven He raised, and He set the balance﴾ [ar-Rahman: 7], there is a great contrast between the raising of the heaven, which is truth, justice and power, and the balance He set on the earth, so that you may stand up with justice and fairness. By this justice the heavens and the earth stand.

In Surat al-Hadid, the balance is linked with the sending of messengers and the sending down of books: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidence and sent down with them the Book and the balance, so that people may maintain justice.﴾ [al-Hadid: 25]

It is well known that the balance sent down with the Book is the balance of truth and justice, and the prohibition of consuming people's wealth unjustly, and of depriving people of their things.

So this verse is the most general and comprehensive of the verses on fulfilling measure and weight, equivalent to His saying: ﴿Indeed, God commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice.﴾ [an-Nisa': 58]

He used the word "trust" in the plural (amanah) to encompass everything a person can be entrusted with.

Likewise here, the balance together with the revealed Book, and by it every person takes his right in any kind of dealing. So whoever cheats in a commodity, or adulterates it, or increases a count, or reduces or increases a measure of length, or reduces, is one who defrauds in measure and falls under the threat of "woe."

For example, whoever sells gold claiming it is pure of alloy, at the weight of one dirham, while it contains one-tenth of a dirham of copper, has reduced and defrauded for himself, taking the right of a full dirham of gold, and he has reduced by giving a dirham less one-tenth.

Whoever sells a ratl (pound) of ghee while it contains one-tenth of a ratl of fat has defrauded to the extent of this tenth for himself, and has reduced and deprived the buyer to the extent of that amount.

(p. 458) Likewise, whoever sells ten meters of cloth while it is short by a quarter of a meter has defrauded and deprived to the extent of this quarter.

Likewise in the division among people, among children, among family members, and in everything in which there is giving and taking between two parties. And God, may He be exalted, knows best.

Among the matters the scholars mention regarding the connections (munasabat) between surahs and one another:

Abu Hayyan said, when he mentioned that the preceding surah concerned the fate of the righteous and the wicked on the Day of Resurrection, that here He mentioned some of the causes of that and the most important of them: defrauding in measure and deficiency in weight. This is generally apt. But the explicit statement of His saying in the preceding surah: ﴿And when the graves are scattered﴾ ﴿Each soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind﴾ [al-Infitar: 4-5], although it is general in everything a person has sent forward of good deeds and what he has delayed of obligatory duties, it also includes in particular what he has sent forward of fulfilling measure and fairness in weight, and what he has delayed of defrauding in measure and depriving others out of greed for wealth and hoarding of inheritance, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And you devour inheritance, devouring greedily﴾ ﴿And you love wealth with immense love﴾ ﴿No! When the earth is ground to powder, pounded and crushed﴾ ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ ﴿And Hell is brought forth that Day. On that Day man will remember, but how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ ﴿He will say: "Oh, I wish I had sent forward for my life."﴾ [al-Fajr: 19-24]

From here it is known to the intelligent person that whatever he has cheated in measure or diminished in weight, however much he has gathered from it, he will leave it behind him, will be held accountable for it, and will regret it, saying: ﴿Oh, I wish I had sent forward for my life.﴾ But by then it is too late for regret.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 83, verse 4:**

The words of God Most High: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected, for a tremendous Day?﴾

This is a rebuke and a reproach to these people. It contains two issues:

The first: The motive behind this conduct is the absence of certainty about the Resurrection. Or certainty exists, but they act as though they were people without certainty, meaning, unconcerned. This is like what the poet said in a similar context, and what rhetoric calls *lazim al-fa'ida* (the implied consequence):

*Shaqiq came, holding his spear across his body. Indeed, the sons of your paternal uncle have spears.*

The speaker knows that Shaqiq is aware that the sons of his paternal uncle have spears, and that they are ready for war (p-459) with him. But he saw in Shaqiq a lack of concern and a lack of preparation, in that he placed his spear in front of him, crosswise. So he is like someone who does not believe that the sons of his uncle have spears. Yet the speaker did not intend, by his words to him, to inform him of something he did not know. Rather, he intended to alert him to what he must do by way of readiness and preparation. The same applies here. This is general for every procrastinator and every lax person, as in the hadith: "The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer," etc.

That is: "while he is a believer" in faith and its implications, including the reward and the reckoning.

The second issue, from the words of God Most High: ﴿the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 6]. It is understood that the one who cheats in measure and weight, while knowing this to be true in most cases, and while the other party does not notice it, has God Most High as the One who observes his act. It is He who will call him to account and examine him, because he betrayed God, to Whom nothing is hidden, glory be to Him. This is why God Most High said: ﴿the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾, and did not say: "the Day when each person will be avenged against his creditor, and every rightful person will receive his right."

A severe warning.

Al-Qurtubi said under this verse: It is reported from Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan that a Bedouin said to him: "You have heard what God said about the defrauders. So what is your opinion of yourself, while you take the wealth of the Muslims without measure or weight?!" End of quote.

This is a statement that should be said to every consumer of people's wealth unjustly, whoever he may be and in whatever way that occurs.

A note.

It is well known that every two parties in a transaction each seek the greater benefit for themselves, so the defrauder must conceal his method from his counterpart.

The scholars of *hisba* (market supervision) mentioned many methods which the ruler in particular should be alert to, and which anyone dealing with others in general should be alert to as well.

Among them, they said: First, regarding the measuring vessel: the body of the vessel may be soft, so one presses it with his hands, its sides come closer together, and what it contains decreases. Therefore the measuring vessel must be rigid, and it is usually made of wood or something equivalent.

Among them: it may be a piece of wood hollowed out from within, but the hollowing does not reach the full required volume. So from the outside it appears large, but from the inside it is small because its bottom is close.

Among them: it may be hollowed to the full required limit, but he places in it something that fills its space at the bottom and fixes it at its base. So what is measured decreases by the amount that fills that space, such as placing paper, rags, plaster, or the like.

Second, regarding the balance: one may file down the weights (*sanj*, the standard weights) until their weight decreases, or hollow out part of them and fill the hollow with a material lighter than them.

Therefore one must regularly inspect the parts of the standard weights. A stone standard may also be used, and it diminishes with frequent use because of what crumbles from it over the days.

Among them: one places under the pan in which he weighs the goods a heavy sticky object, so that the weighed quantity is reduced by the amount of this object.

So that this is not noticed, you will always find him placing the standard weight in the other pan, so that it is the heavier one.

There are many types, such as throwing the goods into the pan with force, so that it tips because of the force of impact, and he takes the goods immediately before it rises back up, deceiving the observer into thinking that it is heavier on the scale.

As for the measuring rod (*dhar'*), the gauge may be complete and accurate, but after he measures the first meter, he pushes the instrument backward and pulls the cloth being measured forward by a handspan, for example. So the deficiency in the cloth equals the amount he pulled of the fabric.

All these are matters that may be hidden from many people. I once observed a seller with one of the scales that he held in his hand, and he repeated the weighing five times, each time with a method different from the other, until he exhausted what he had. Then he turned to me and said: "I do not sell at this price." I said to him: "Take what you want and weigh as I want." He asked for double the price. I gave it to him, and he handed me the scale so that I could weigh with my own hands.

Here we should alert to the situations of sellers: when the price is high and you find a seller selling cheaply, this may be due to a defect in the weight or in the goods, or to harm to the other party.

Another note.

Because of these causes, their realities, and the severity of their danger, Umar, may God be pleased with him, used to tour the market himself and inspect the measure and the scale. He would expel from the market whoever he found deficient in his measure or his weight, and he would say: "Do not withhold the rain from us."

Thus it is incumbent upon rulers to continually inspect this, especially in lands where religious restraint is weak and prices are high, which drives sellers to trickery or obstinacy.

Umar prevented a raisin seller from selling cheaply, because he knew that a merchant had arrived with a large quantity of raisins. It was said to Umar: "Why did you prohibit selling at a low price?" He said: "Because it spoils the market, so the newcomer will suffer losses and refrain from bringing goods to Madinah, while this one has profited before."

Another note.

It should be known that the type and quantity of the measure, and the type and quantity of the weight, are referred to the sultan (ruler). As the scholars of *hisba* said: the community must obey the ruler in four matters: the type of measure and weight, the type of currency he issues for transactions, and the declaration of war or the acceptance of peace.

So if he adopts the *sa'* (a volume measure), the *mudd* (a volume measure), the *kayla* (a measure), the *wayba* (a measure), or the *qadah* (a measure), or any type, large or small, then it is obligatory to abide by it in the markets.

Likewise with weight: whether he adopts the *dirham*, the *uqiyya* (ounce), the *ratl* (pound), or the *uqqa*, or adopts the gram and the kilogram, all of these are his prerogative.

As for when the matter is between two people in a division, for example, the division of a heap of grain, if they agree to divide it using a large vessel for speed, provided it is standardized, not varying from one time to another by being rigid and capable of measuring, then that is permissible.

Or likewise with weight: they agree on a specific piece of iron, of which each one's share is a number of times its weight, then there is no harm in that, because the purpose is the division of the whole, not an exchange on the basis of the parts.

(p-462) As for the basic Islamic measures and weights, their explanation was previously given by the Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and him, in the chapter on zakat on what comes out of the earth and the zakat on the two precious metals. We also presented their equivalents in modern weight in the chapter on zakat al-fitr, at the words of God Most High: ﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right, for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 24-25]. And success is from God Most High.

A rare note.

On the night I finished writing this section, I saw the Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and him, in a dream. After he left me, I saw someone who said to me: "Defrauding in measure and weight has a connection to usury (*riba*)." So I added it at the beginning of the section, after I had reflected on it and found it correct because of the disparity (*mufadala*) involved.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 83, verse 14:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Nay! Rather, what they have been earning has covered over their hearts.﴾

"Raana" (رانَ): means "covered over," as in the hadith: "When the servant commits a sin, a black spot is marked on his heart, and it continues thus until it covers it," the hadith.

The poet said:

؎ "How many a sin has covered over the heart of a wicked man, so he repented of the sin that had covered over him, and became clear."

Abu Hayyan said: The root of ar-rayn (الرَّيْنِ) is domination (al-ghalabah). It is said: "The wine overcame (raanat) the intellect of its drinker and grew strong":

؎ "Then when he saw it, the wine overcame him, and it prevented him from seeing by its absence."

An explanation of the recitations in this verse:

Abu Hayyan said: It was recited "bal raana" with the assimilation of the lam into the ra' (idgham), and with clear pronunciation (izhar). Hafs paused on "bal" with a light, brief pause so that the clear pronunciation would be distinct.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Badhish said: The reciters agreed upon the assimilation of the lam into the ra', except for Hafs's pause on "bal" and then saying "raana."

What he mentioned is as he mentioned regarding the consensus.

However, in the book "al-Lawami'," from Qalun through all his transmission routes: clear pronunciation of the lam before the ra', such as His saying: (p-463) ﴿Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself﴾ [an-Nisa': 158] and "bal rabbukum" [al-Anbiya': 56].

In the book of Ibn 'Atiyyah: "Nafi' recited 'bal raana' without assimilation."

In it also: Nafi' also recited with assimilation and imalah.

Sibawayh said: Clear pronunciation and assimilation are both good.

Az-Zamakhshari said: It was recited with assimilation of the lam into the ra', and clear pronunciation and assimilation are better; and the alif was inclined (imalah) and emphasized (tafkhim). Ended.

As for the meaning, the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has previously given a full explanation of it in Surah al-Kahf, when discussing His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it﴾ [al-Kahf: 57], the verse.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah At-Tatfif (The Defrauders)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay! Indeed, from their Lord, that Day, they will be veiled.﴾

It is understood from this that the believers will not be veiled from their Lord on the Day of Resurrection. We have already mentioned the way of reconciling this understanding with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him﴾ [6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 83, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Its seal is musk, and for this let the strivers strive﴾

This is a direction toward that in which competition (al-munafasah) ought to be, and it means desire for a thing (al-raghbah fi al-shay').

Abu Hayyan said: "Nafasa fi al-shay'" means he desired it. "Nafistu 'alayhi bi al-shay' unfisu nafasatan" means that when you are stingy with the thing toward him and do not like that it should come into his possession.

What appears to me, and God the Exalted knows best, is that this is from seeking after and vying for a precious thing, so that each one hastens toward it in order to take it for himself.

In this noble verse there is a reminder back to the beginning of the surah: if those people strive to gather wealth through short-measuring (al-tatfif), then for them is woe on the Day of Resurrection.

And if the righteous (al-abrar) are in bliss on the Day of Resurrection, and this is their drink, then this is the true place of competition, not in short-measuring of grain or any measured or weighed good.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 83, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾ ﴿And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks﴾.

Their being described here as criminals (ijram) indicates that this is the cause of their laughing at the believers and winking at them. (p-464) Another reason was explained earlier in Surah "al-Baqarah," in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they ridicule those who believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 212].

In Surah "al-Baqarah," Allah, exalted is He, has also made clear that those who had taqwa will be above them on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, spoke about this there, and referred to this verse for the explanation of the type of mockery. He expanded the explanation in Surah "al-Ahqaf" on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 11].

Among the motives for their saying this, and its consequence, he cited the verses of Surah "al-Mutaffifin" at that point, and likewise at the beginning of Surah "al-Waqi'ah," on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 3].

It is worth noting that this condition is not specific to this nation; rather, it was previously pointed out that it occurs among other nations before it.

Regarding the people of Noah: ﴿And he was building the ark, and whenever a group of the chiefs of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾ [Hud: 38].

The same response was given to them: ﴿He said, "If you mock us, indeed we mock you as you mock. And you will know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment"﴾ [Hud: 38-39].

He also brought what conveys even more than that, including the messengers, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to mock﴾ [al-An'am: 10].

A similar statement appears in Surah "al-Anbiya'" with the same wording of the verse mentioned.

Warning.

If this is the condition of some of those who committed crimes toward some weak believers, and likewise the condition of some nations toward their messengers, then the caller to Allah, exalted is He, must not be affected by the mockery of anyone toward him, and must know that he is upon the same path as other callers to Allah, exalted is He, and that Allah, exalted is He, will support him, either soon or later, as is found at the end of every context of these verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 83, verse 34:

(p-465) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ ﴿upon couches, looking on﴾ ﴿Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?﴾

This is a rebuttal of the mockery the polytheists directed at the believers in this world. It is as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿But those who feared Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Baqarah: 212].

The explanation of this by the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) was given earlier, in surah al-Mu'minun, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience; indeed, they are the triumphant﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 111]. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
